Bat control

Pitch and handedness apply on the next ball. Two-finger input uses scroll gestures. Pinch-to-zoom is kept separate.
BATTING, BY INSTINCT

Position. Read. Swing.

Mouse: move freely over the pitch to position the bat. Pull down for backlift; stroke upward to drive forward. A quicker stroke creates more bat speed. No click is needed.

Windows touchpad: choose Two fingers in Controls. Slide two fingers sideways to set the line, pull back, then swipe forward. If movement feels reversed, enable Invert. Rest your fingers between strokes.

Touchscreen: drag to move the bat and swipe forward to swing. One or two fingers work.

Look around: hold the right mouse button and move, or press L / tap Look to switch to neck look. Use C / Center to return to the bowler. Look down for pads and shoes; look over your shoulder for the keeper. A standard gamepad right stick also controls the view.

Training pace: Set Bowling Speed changes the next release, including fixed, random and progressive speed. No airborne ball is altered.

Keyboard: WASD adjusts your guard, hold X to advance down the pitch, Q/E rotates the face, Shift adds loft, Enter swings, Space leaves, and P pauses.

Contact is physical: the bat must meet the ball. There are no advance delivery labels or landing hints. Replay and measurements appear only after the ball.

Development nets: pitch and aerodynamic values are uncalibrated priors. Field players are visual only. This slice has no running, catches, LBW or official match format.
